title: AVAir 3378
summary: AVAir Flight 3378 departed Raleigh-Durham at 21:25 on an IFR flight to Richmond in low ceiling, low visibility conditions. Shortly after takeoff during initial climb to 300 feet, the aircraft executed an excessive rate of turn instead of maintaining standard climb profile. The first officer was flying while the captain communicated with ATC. The aircraft descended in a 45-degree turn and struck a reservoir, impacting with water then continuing onto land.
probable_cause: The failure of flight crew to maintain a proper flightpath. Contributing factors were the ineffective management and supervision of flight crew training and operations and inappropriate FAA surveillance of AVAir.

factors.evidence: Ceiling 100 feet AGL, visibility 2400 feet RVR, fog condition (p. 2)
Improper instrument scanning and visual/aural perception by copilot/second pilot; pilot in command with inadequate monitoring (p. 2, Finding #5, #9, #13)

Company records showed instances of substandard performance by first officer; inadequate surveillance of operation and training by company/operator management; inadequate FAA surveillance (p. 1, Finding #6, #7, #73, #74)
Aircraft in 45-degree descending turn during initial climb; inadvertent descent by copilot (p. 1, Finding #1, #14)
Aircraft struck water in reservoir and continued onto land (p. 1)

events.text: AVAir Flight 3378 departed Raleigh-Durham International Airport under IFR in low ceiling, low visibility, night conditions (p. 1, 2)
First officer as pilot flying; captain handling ATC communications (p. 1)
Aircraft climbed to 300 feet maintaining appropriate climb speed (p. 1)
Aircraft began excessive rate of turn of 40 to 45 degrees instead of standard 22 degrees (p. 1)
Radar analysis indicated aircraft was in 45-degree descending turn; aircraft descended inadvertently (p. 1, Finding #14)
Aircraft struck water in reservoir approximately 100 feet from shoreline (p. 1)
Aircraft continued impact trajectory from water onto land into forested area (p. 1)
Aircraft destroyed with all 12 occupants (2 crew, 10 passengers) fatally injured; on-ground fire occurred (p. 1)
